questions.question: Which Chinese traveller visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hsuan Tsang.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Chinese traveller** who visited India during the **reign of Harshavardhana** was **Hsuan Tsang,** also known as **Xuanzang.**
 
• He came to India in the** 7th century** and stayed here for **14 years**, during which he** travelled extensively **and wrote about his experiences in his book **"The Great Tang Records on the Western Regions".**
 
• Hsuan Tsang was a **Buddhist monk** and his main purpose of visiting India was to study **Buddhism and collect Buddhist texts.**
 
• He visited many important Buddhist sites in India, including** Bodh Gaya, **where he meditated under the **Bodhi tree** and studied Buddhist philosophy under the guidance of a famous **Indian monk, Shilabhadra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options mentioned in the question are **not relevant** to the reign of Harshavardhana.
 
• **Faxian** was a **Chinese Buddhist monk** who visited India in the **5th century.**
 
• **Etsing **is** not** a known Chinese traveller, and** Ibn Battuta **was a** Moroccan explorer** who visited India in the **14th century.**
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 1.

questions.question: Thomas Cup is a/an ____________.

questions.question: Which is the only living representative of Sphenopsida that has an underground, creeping and perennial rhizome that gives off aerial as well as underground branches?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equisetum.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is** option 4, Equisetum**, which is commonly known as** horsetail or scouring rush.**
 
• Equisetum has an **underground, creeping and perennial rhizome** that gives off **aerial **as well as** underground branches**.
 
• It is the only living representative of **Sphenopsida**, a group of **vascular plants **that were dominant during the **Carboniferous period.**
 
• **Adiantum**, also known as** maidenhair fern,** belongs to the group of **ferns **and **does no**t have an underground rhizome.
 
 
• It has **delicate fronds** and is commonly grown as an** ornamental plant.**
 
 
 
• **Dryopteris** is another **group of ferns** that **does not** have an underground rhizome.
 
 
• It is commonly known as **wood fern **and is also grown as an **ornamental plant.**
 
 
 
• **Selaginella, **also known as **spike moss,** is a group of plants that are **similar to ferns** but have** smaller leaves** and are adapted to grow in** dry environments.**
 
 
• They **do not** have an underground rhizome.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0f43c31587a372f5a7ce0db582a061e8322aa1ad07f7bc85d4b2c70866286b5.png] 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equisetum** is a **unique plant** that has been used for** medicinal purposes **for centuries.

 
 
• It contains **silica **and other minerals that are believed to have **anti-inflammatory and diuretic properties.**
 
 
 
• **Adiantum** is also used in **traditional medicine** to treat **respiratory and digestive problems.**
 
 
• It is also used in **hair care products** because of its **high silica content.**
 
 
 
• **Dryopteris **is commonly used in landscaping because of its** attractive foliage **and** tolerance to shade.**
 
• **Selaginella** is used in** terrariums and indoor gardens** because of its **small size and unique appearance.**

questions.question: Trichloromethane is better known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chloroform.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trichloromethane** is better known as **Chloroform.**
 
• Chloroform is a **colorless liquid** with a **sweet odor** and a **nonflammable nature.**
 
• It is commonly used as an **anesthetic during surgeries** and medical procedures.
 
• Chloroform was also used as a** solvent **and in the production of** refrigerants and pesticides**.
 
• However, its use has been restricted due to its** potential toxicity** and **carcinogenic effects**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Butanes**

 
 
• Butanes are a group of **hydrocarbons** that are commonly used as **fuel for lighters and stoves.**
 
• They are also used as **propellants** in **aerosol sprays** and as a **refrigerant.**
 
• However, they are **highly flammable** and can pose a **fire hazard** if not handled properly.
 
 
 
• **LPG**
 
 
• LPG or liquefied petroleum gas is a mixture of **propane and butane.**
 
• It is commonly used as fuel for **heating, cooking, and transportation.**
 
• LPG is a** clean-burning fuel** and emits **fewer pollutants **compared to other fossil fuels.
 
• However, it is** highly flammable **and can **pose safety risks **if not handled properly.
 
 
 
• **Laughing gas**
 
 
• Laughing gas is the common name for **nitrous oxide**, which is a **colorless gas** with a **sweet odor.**
 
• It is commonly used as an **anesthetic **during **dental procedures **and as a **recreational drug.**
 
• Nitrous oxide has a **euphoric effect **and can cause **laughing and giggling**, hence the name.
 
• However, it can also cause** dizziness, nausea, **and in rare cases,** loss of consciousness.**

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment added Fundamental Duties in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forty - Second Amendment Act, 1976.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Fundamental Duties** were added to the Constitution by the **Forty-Second Amendment Act of 1976.**
 
• The Fundamental Duties are a set of **moral obligations** and** responsibilities **that every citizen of India is expected to follow.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the **Constitution of the Soviet Union.**
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of the** Swaran Singh Committee.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Constitution (Forty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1984,** this amendment included 14 land reform acts in the Ninth Schedule.The states of **Assam, Bihar, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal, **as well as the union territories of **Goa, Daman, and Diu, passed these laws**
 
• **Forty-Fourth Amendment Act of 1978 **primarily focused on restoring provisions that were changed by the** 42nd Amendment Act**, particularly regarding fundamental rights, the powers of the President and the judiciary, and emergency provisions.

questions.question: What are the main energy sources for earth's internal heat engine?

options.text: Radiogenic heat and oceanic tide heat
Heat from volcanoes and solar heat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiogenic heat and primordial heat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The main energy sources for** earth's internal heat engine** are r**adiogenic heat and primordial heat.**
 
• Radiogenic heat is produced by the **decay of radioactive isotopes** in the earth's crust and mantle.
 
• **Primordial heat **is the heat left over from the **formation of the earth.**
 
• These two sources are the **main contributors **to earth's internal heat engine.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts was introduced to regulate Foreign Exchange in India in 1973?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**FERA.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) **was introduced in India in** 1973** to regulate **foreign exchange transactions **and to **conserve foreign exchange reserves.**
 
• **FERA** was replaced by the **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) in 1999**, which was introduced to **simplify and liberalize** the foreign exchange regime in India.
 
• The** Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act** was introduced in** 2003** to ensure** fiscal discipline** and reduce the **fiscal deficit** of the Indian government.
 
• The** Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act** was introduced in **2002** to provide a legal framework for **banks and financial institutions** to recover their **non-performing assets. **
 
• **Option 1, **FERA, is the correct answer to the question asked as it was the act introduced in **1973 **to regulate foreign exchange in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **FERA** was considered a **stringent act** as it imposed restrictions on **foreign exchange transactions **and punished offenders with **fines and imprisonment.**
 
• **FEMA,** which replaced FERA, is a more liberal act that allows for **easier foreign exchange transactions **and investments in India.
 
• **FRBM** sets targets for the government to **reduce the fiscal deficit **to a certain percentage of the GDP and also sets targets for the** reduction of public debt. **
 
• **SARFAESI **gives banks and financial institutions the power to **seize and sell assets of defaulting borrowers **without court intervention.

questions.question: Which German chemist and physicist proposed that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons, Which can mathematically be written as 4n + 2 (n = 0,1,2,3, etc.) in 1931?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Erich Huckel.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **German chemist and physicist** who proposed that an **aromatic compound** must have an **odd number** of pairs of **electrons,** which can mathematically be written as **4n + 2 (n = 0,1,2,3, etc.) in 1931** is** Erich Huckel. **
 
• Huckel's rule helps in determining whether a compound is **aromatic** or not by checking the number of** pairs of electrons **in its **pi system.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Friedrich Kekule **was a **German chemist** who proposed the structure of **benzene in 1865**, which is a** six-membered aromatic ring** with alternating double bonds.
 
• **Rosalind Franklin** was a **British biophysicist **who played a crucial role in discovering the **structure of DNA.**
 
• **Antoine Lavoisier** was a **French chemist **who is considered the **father of modern chemistry **for his work in understanding the nature of **combustion and oxygen's **role in it.
 
• Hence, the statement is correct, and **Erich Huckel **is the German chemist and physicist who proposed **Huckel's rule in 1931.**

questions.question: Nag Panchami is celebrated in which month of Hindu Calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shravan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nag Panchami **is a **Hindu festival** dedicated to the **worship of snakes**, which is celebrated on the** fifth day of the bright half **of the** lunar month of Shravan.**
 
• The festival is celebrated in various parts of India, especially in states like **Maharashtra, Karnataka, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is believed that **worshipping snakes** on this day will bring** good luck and prosperity** to the family.
 
• People offer** milk, flowers, and sweets** to the idols of snakes and also visit** temples** dedicated to **Nagas (the serpent deities).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word** 'Nag'** means** snake or serpent** in Sanskrit, and **'Panchami'** refers to the** fifth day **of the** lunar fortnight.**
 
• In some regions, people also observe a** fast on Nag Panchami **and break it after **offering prayers** to the snakes.
 
• In **West Bengal,** the festival is celebrated as** Manasa Puja**, dedicated to the goddess of **snakes, Manasa Devi.**
 
• In **Maharashtra,** people decorate their homes with **rangoli **and offer a special dish called '**kanda bhaji'** to the snakes.
 
• **Kartik** is the** eighth month **of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **October-November.**
 
 
• It is known for several festivals like **Diwali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.**
 
 
 
• **Sharad** is the season of **autumn**, which falls between **September and November**.
 
 
• It is known for festivals like **Navratri, Durga Puja, and Vijayadashami.**
 
 
 
• **Asadh** is the 4th month of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **June-July**.
 
 
• It is known for the beginning of the** monsoon season** and several **agricultural festivals.**

questions.question: ______________ became the first swimmer from India to breach the Olympic Qualification Time (A cut) in swimming as he capped the qualification period with an outstanding performance in the Sette Colli Trophy in Rome, Italy in June 2021.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sajan Prakash.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sajan Prakash** became the** first swimmer** from India to breach the **Olympic Qualification Time (**A cut) in swimming in **June 2021.**
 
• He achieved this feat in the **Sette Colli Trophy** in **Rome, Italy.**
 
• Sajan Prakash clocked **1:56.38s **in the **200m butterfly event**, which is** below **the Olympic Qualification Time (A cut) of **1:56.48s.**
 
• At Tokyo 2020, Sajan Prakash, who also swam at Rio 2016, is set to become the first Indian swimmer to participate in two Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srihari Nataraj, Anand Anilkumar Shylaja, and Virdhawal Khade** are also well-known Indian swimmers, but they have** not** breached the Olympic Qualification Time (A cut) in swimming as of **June 2021.**

questions.question: Who is the regulator of Micro Finance Institutions in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBI.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the **central bank** of India, which regulates the **functioning of banks** and other financial institutions in the country.
 
• RBI is also responsible for **regulating and supervising **the **microfinance institutions (MFIs)** in India, which provide** small loans** to the** low-income households and micro-entrepreneurs.**
 
• RBI has issued guidelines for the** registration and operation of MFIs**, and it also monitors their **compliance** with the **regulatory norms.**
 
• RBI has set up a dedicated department for the supervision of** NBFC-MFIs (Non-Banking Financial Company-Microfinance Institutions),** which are the main type of MFIs in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)** is the regulator of the** securities market **in India, which oversees the functioning of** stock exchanges, mutual funds, and other market intermediaries.**
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)** is a development bank, which provides** financial and technical assistance** to the **agriculture and rural sectors** in India.
 
• **SBI (State Bank of India)** is a **public sector bank**, which is one of the largest banks in India.
 
 
• However, it is **not** the regulator of MFIs in India.
 
 
 
• Hence, the statement "The regulator of Micro Finance Institutions in India is RBI" is** correct.**
